sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: I'm Gemma Spake, and welcome back to The Psychology of Your 20s, the podcast where we talk through the biggest changes, experiences, moments, and transitions of our 20s
sentences.zh: 我是杰玛·斯派克，欢迎回到《你的二十多岁心理学》，在这里我们探讨二十多岁时最大的改变、经历、时刻和转折，

sentences.en: and what they mean for our psychology.
sentences.zh: 以及它们对我们心理的意义。

sentences.en: Hello, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本节目。

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到本播客。

sentences.en: And thank you for joining me for another episode as we break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 感谢大家收听又一期节目，和我们一起剖析二十多岁的心理学。

sentences.en: So today I want to talk about this kind of, this idea or theory that I've been playing around with and exploring in kind of recent months.
sentences.zh: 所以今天我想聊聊我最近几个月一直在思考和探索的一种观点或理论。

sentences.en: I talk a lot about the quarter-life crisis on this podcast, which is, you know, the period in our early to mid-20s when we're just struck by all these compounding questions
sentences.zh: 我在这个播客里经常谈到四分之一人生危机，也就是你在二十岁出头到中旬时，突然被各种层出不穷的问题

sentences.en: and fears all at once, and it feels like everything is going wrong.
sentences.zh: 和恐惧同时击中，感觉一切都在出问题。

sentences.en: We have no sense of stability, no sense of direction, purpose.
sentences.zh: 我们没有丝毫的稳定性，没有方向感，也没有目标。

sentences.en: Our lives are falling apart, but equally we feel like our lives are just starting and we're the oldest we've ever been, we're the youngest we've ever been.
sentences.zh: 我们的生活正在崩塌，但与此同时，我们又觉得生活才刚开始，我们既是有生以来最年长的，又是历年来最年轻的。

sentences.en: It's like this crazy moment.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一个疯狂的时刻。

sentences.en: It's a rite of passage, even though it feels like no one else has ever experienced it before.
sentences.zh: 这是一个成长仪式，尽管感觉好像从来没有人经历过这一切。

sentences.en: And it's very terrifying because we kind of hope to exit it as quickly as it starts, and we hope that we exit it better than how we entered it.
sentences.zh: 这非常吓人，因为我们希望能像它开始时那样快地走出来，并且希望我们出来时能比进去时更好。

sentences.en: That's our quarter-life crisis.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的四分之一人生危机。

sentences.en: We kind of have no guarantee of where it's taking us, but we just kind of have to have hope.
sentences.zh: 我们有点无法保证它会把我们带向何方，但我们只能怀抱希望。

sentences.en: The quarter-life crisis, you know, is a lot about shedding old things and the destruction of an old life.
sentences.zh: 你知道，四分之一人生危机很大程度上关乎抛弃旧事物和旧生活的毁灭。

sentences.en: But there's this other phenomena that accompanies it that I think is spoken about less, mainly because, A, it's very subtle,
sentences.zh: 但伴随它的还有另一种现象，我觉得大家讨论得比较少，主要是因为：第一，它非常微妙；

sentences.en: and B, it's something that can only be recognized in hindsight.
sentences.zh: 第二，它只有在事后才能被认出来。

sentences.en: And it's the idea of the quarter-life reinvention.
sentences.zh: 这就是四分之一人生重塑的概念。

sentences.en: This thing I have seen time and time again where people emerge from their quarter-life crisis at 26, 27, 28, maybe even in the 30s,
sentences.zh: 我一次又一次地看到这种现象：人们在26、27、28岁，甚至30多岁时从四分之一人生危机中走出来，

sentences.en: completely different people to who they were at 22, 23, 24.
sentences.zh: 变得与22、23、24岁时的自己判若两人。

sentences.en: And it's not just normal development.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是正常的发展。

sentences.en: Something intrinsic shifts in them, but also physical and emotional.
sentences.zh: 他们身上发生了本质上的转变，同时也是生理和情感上的。

sentences.en: And at the tail end of the quarter-life crisis, they get this almost second puberty or second growth spurt that completely changes the trajectory of their lives,
sentences.zh: 在四分之一人生危机的尾声，他们会迎来几乎是第二次青春期或第二次生长爆发，彻底改变了他们人生的轨迹，

sentences.en: psychologically and emotionally.
sentences.zh: 在心理和情感上都是如此。

sentences.en: Unlike, again, like I said, the quarter-life crisis, which is depicted as the collapse, the quarter-life reinvention is the expansion and growth of something.
sentences.zh: 再次强调，正如我所说，四分之一人生危机被描绘为一种崩溃，而四分之一人生重塑则是某种事物的扩张与成长。

sentences.en: And it is this transformation that seems to only be able to take place when everything unnecessary has fallen away.
sentences.zh: 而且这种转变似乎只有在所有不必要的东西都剥落之后才会发生。

sentences.en: So I want to talk about it today.
sentences.zh: 所以我今天想聊聊这个。

sentences.en: I want to talk about the psychology behind it, the phases that we move through when we go through a quarter-life crisis, and how to know when you are getting close
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈它背后的心理学，我们在经历四分之一人生危机时所经历的阶段，以及如何知道自己何时接近

sentences.en: to the reinvention stage, how to get yourself there, not faster, but with less friction and what to expect.
sentences.zh: 重塑阶段，如何到达那里——不是靠加速，而是减少摩擦，以及该有什么样的期待。

sentences.en: So without further ado, let's get into the psychology of the quarter-life reinvention.
sentences.zh: 所以废话不多说，让我们进入四分之一人生重塑的心理学。

sentences.en: So the idea of the quarter-life crisis, I know I've kind of explained it already, but I think it's one we're fairly familiar with.
sentences.zh: 关于四分之一人生危机的概念，我知道我已经解释过了，但我认为这是我们相当熟悉的一个概念。

sentences.en: It is a distinct period in our lives where we experience a rapid onset of confusion, self-doubt, and anxiety that we aren't living our lives as we should be.
sentences.zh: 这是我们生命中的一个特定阶段，我们会经历一阵迅速袭来的困惑、自我怀疑和焦虑，觉得自己没有过上应有的生活。

sentences.en: I think the kind of fantasy and ease of our childhood, of our teen years, of our early adulthood, seems to just like slip away overnight.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们童年、青少年时期以及步入成年早期的那种幻想和轻松感，似乎在一夜之间就溜走了。

sentences.en: And we basically realize almost all at once, like, wait a second, like this is getting very serious.
sentences.zh: 我们几乎同时意识到，“等一下，这变得非常严肃了。”

sentences.en: And soon after we are like, well, if this is getting serious, do I want to be in the life this is leading me to?
sentences.zh: 不久之后我们就会想：“好吧，如果这变得很严肃，我真的想过上这把导向的生活吗？”

sentences.en: It's definitely going to cause you to examine a whole lot.
sentences.zh: 这绝对会促使你做全方位的审视。

sentences.en: And there is a choice.
sentences.zh: 这里面临着一个选择。

sentences.en: Keep going this way or pivot, redirect, change.
sentences.zh: 继续这样走下去，还是转向、重定向、改变。

sentences.en: The choice to redirect or the moments where we feel forced to redirect are where a lot of the tension and the anxiety come from.
sentences.zh: 重定向的选择，或者我们感到被迫重定向的时刻，正是许多紧张感和焦虑的来源。

sentences.en: It borrows its name, the quarter-life crisis borrows its name from the more widely known, well, I don't even think it's more widely known anymore, but the original idea
sentences.zh: 这个词借用了更广为人知的——好吧，我觉得它现在甚至不算更广为人知了，但它是最初关于

sentences.en: of the midlife crisis.
sentences.zh: 中年危机的概念。

sentences.en: The midlife crisis was a critical life stage first observed by the psychologist
sentences.zh: 中年危机是心理学家

sentences.en: Elliot Schach in the 1960s who kind of stood in front of this
sentences.zh: 埃利奥特·雅克（Elliott Jaques）在20世纪60年代首次观察到的一个关键人生阶段，他当时站在

sentences.en: cohort of British psychologists and said,
sentences.zh: 一群英国心理学家面前说，

sentences.en: all of us, a lot of people are going to go through this period at midlife where they get really depressed and they get really unhappy and we need to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 我们所有人，许多人都会在中年时期经历这样一个阶段，他们会变得非常沮丧和不快乐，我们需要谈谈这件事。

sentences.en: And he had seen it time and time again in patience.
sentences.zh: 他在病人身上一次又一次地看到这种情况。

sentences.en: He'd read about it in biographies.
sentences.zh: 他在传记中读到过。

sentences.en: He'd observed it in himself and family and friends.
sentences.zh: 他在自己、家人和朋友身上都观察到了这一点。

sentences.en: People reached what he called the crest of the hill, the halfway point of life and realized their trajectory so far had been up and up and up and now inevitably
sentences.zh: 人们达到了他所谓的“山脊”，也就是人生的中点，并意识到他们到目前为止的人生轨迹一直在上升、上升、上升，而现在

sentences.en: they're at the top of the hill, they're halfway through life and it's all down.
sentences.zh: 不可避免地，他们来到了山顶，走到了人生的中点，接下来全是下坡路。

sentences.en: It's leading towards death.
sentences.zh: 它正通向死亡。

sentences.en: The years are fewer in front than behind.
sentences.zh: 面前剩下的年份比身后的要少。

sentences.en: It's a very existential moment for many people and he observed people doing very irrational things, very strange things to maintain their sense of youth.
sentences.zh: 对许多人来说，这是一个非常具有存在主义色彩的时刻，他观察到人们为了保持青春感而做出非常不理智、非常奇怪的事情。

sentences.en: Suddenly they're leaving marriages with people they seem to love.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，他们离开了看似深爱着的伴侣。

sentences.en: Suddenly they're spending all their savings on ridiculous things like red sports cars.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，他们把所有的积蓄花在红色跑车这种荒谬的事情上。

sentences.en: They're having these out of the blue.
sentences.zh: 这些都是毫无征兆的。

sentences.en: They're quitting their jobs and doing crazy stuff is what he said.
sentences.zh: 正如他所说，他们辞掉工作，做一些疯狂的事情。

sentences.en: And so he originally only identified one point like this in our life and then people kind of took that idea and they said wait a second I think this happens more than once.
sentences.zh: 所以他最初只在我们的人生中确定了这样一个点，然后人们采用了这个想法说：“等一下，我觉得这不止发生一次。”

sentences.en: Eric Erickson, the famous psychologist said I think this happens in our 20s but it didn't really gain traction for a while that it would happen during our 20s.
sentences.zh: 著名心理学家埃里克·埃里克森（Eric Erickson）说，我认为这发生在我们的20多岁，但它在20多岁时发生这一说法并没有立即流行起来。

sentences.en: People thought people were too young but then as our life expectancy increased you know the global average has gone from 52 in the 60s to like 74.
sentences.zh: 人们觉得大家还太年轻，但随着我们的预期寿命增加，你知道，全球平均寿命从60年代的52岁上升到了74岁左右。

sentences.en: These days that's a 40% difference if I have my math correct.
sentences.zh: 如果我的数学没算错的话，如今这有40%的差距。

sentences.en: Like when that happened people were like okay yeah this is more distinct.
sentences.zh: 当这种情况发生时，人们就像是：好吧，确实，这更加明显了。

sentences.en: There is a crisis that happens around around our 20s that we can't ignore.
sentences.zh: 在我们的20多岁左右确实会发生一场我们无法忽视的危机。

sentences.en: There's just simply more life to worry about we're going to have more moments of crisis.
sentences.zh: 需要担心的生活变多了，我们会有更多感到危机的时刻。

sentences.en: What we realize now and what I have to give credit for to the authors
sentences.zh: 我们现在所意识到的，以及我必须感谢作家

sentences.en: Alexander Robbins and Abby Wilner for articulating for the first time in their book
sentences.zh: 亚历山大·罗宾斯（Alexander Robbins）和艾比·威尔纳（Abby Wilner）在他们的书中首次阐明的是，

sentences.en: The Quarter Life Crisis is that life is not this big clump of years stretching out before us one after the other often just slightly different but mostly the same.
sentences.zh: 《四分之一人生危机》（The Quarter Life Crisis），生活并不是一大团连绵延伸的年份，一个接一个，通常只略有不同但大同小异。

sentences.en: There are these inflection points where things change rapidly all at once and our identity our future our hopes and dreams seem to just be flipped because of things
sentences.zh: 这里存在着一些拐点，事情会在瞬间急剧变化，由于我们控制之内和之外的事情，我们的身份、未来、希望和梦想似乎都被颠覆了。

sentences.en: within and outside of our control.
sentences.zh: 由于我们控制之内和之外的事情。

sentences.en: Like a breakup grief losing a job like you move to a new place and then six months pass and you're like who am I?
sentences.zh: 比如分手、悲伤、失业，比如你搬到一个新地方，然后六个月过去了，你在想：“我是谁？”

sentences.en: Like who am I?
sentences.zh: “我是谁？”

sentences.en: I don't even recognize who I was six months ago.
sentences.zh: 我甚至认不出六个月前的自己了。

sentences.en: All these things can trigger this cascade of other changes and with it a complete instability and a reassessment of like what do I want from my life?
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情都会引发一连串的其他变化，并带来彻底的不稳定性以及对“我对生活有什么期望？”的重新评估。

sentences.en: Who am I?
sentences.zh: “我是谁？”

sentences.en: What am I doing here?
sentences.zh: “我在这里做什么？”

sentences.en: That's the Quarter Life Crisis and it's a funny thing because it's not just contained to a couple of years at 22 or 23.
sentences.zh: 这就是四分之一人生危机，这很有趣，因为它不仅限于22岁或23岁的短短几年。

sentences.en: It can be experienced as young as 18.
sentences.zh: 它最早可以在18岁时经历。

sentences.en: It can last for seven plus years or more and something I rarely see spoken about is that you can have more than one Quarter Life Crisis.
sentences.zh: 它可以持续七年甚至更久，而且我很少听到有人谈论的是，你可能会经历不止一次四分之一人生危机。

sentences.en: In fact you will likely have a couple two in fact and they're very very different.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你很可能会经历几次，准确地说是两次，而且它们非常非常不同。

sentences.en: This 2019 paper published in the journal Emerging
sentences.zh: 这篇2019年发表在《新兴成年期》（Emerging Adulthood）期刊上的论文

sentences.en: Adulthood found that these two distinct types of
sentences.zh: 发现这两种不同类型的

sentences.en: Quarter Life Crisis are called the
sentences.zh: 四分之一人生危机被称为

sentences.en: Locked Out and the Locked In
sentences.zh: “被锁在外”和“被锁在内”

sentences.en: Quarter Life Crisis.
sentences.zh: 四分之一人生危机。

sentences.en: The Locked In
sentences.zh: “被锁在内”

sentences.en: Kind is when you feel trapped in your circumstances and you just like don't know how to change.
sentences.zh: 这种是指你觉得自己被困在当前的环境中，却不知道该如何改变。

sentences.en: The Locked Out
sentences.zh: “被锁在外”

sentences.en: Kind is when you know you need to change but you don't know how to access the next part of your life that you want.
sentences.zh: 这种是指你知道自己需要改变，但不知道如何触及你想要的下一个人生阶段。

sentences.en: You have a better idea of your desired life you just don't know how to get there and both of these moments are equally crisis creating.
sentences.zh: 你对理想的生活有了更好的想法，只是不知道如何达到，而这两种时刻同样都会制造危机。

sentences.en: When I reflect on you know my own life
sentences.zh: 当我回想我自己的生活，

sentences.en: when I reflect on my own life but yeah when I do I can see these two types of crises so distinctly especially in hindsight you know I
sentences.zh: 当我回想我自己的生活时——是的，当我这样做时，我能非常清晰地看到这两种类型的危机，尤其是在事后回想时，你知道的，我

sentences.en: went through such a confusing period maybe like three or four years ago where it was just like none of this is working nothing is changing I feel stuck here I don't want to be
sentences.zh: 经历了这样一个令人困惑的时期，大概是三四年前吧，当时的感觉就是：这些全都没用，什么都没变，我觉得自己被困在这里了，我不想呆在

sentences.en: here I don't know what I want I was working a corporate job I was dating these like quite frankly like these losers I didn't really exercise I didn't really have
sentences.zh: 这里，我不知道自己想要什么。我当时在一家公司上班，约会的对象说实话就是些废柴，我不怎么锻炼，我几乎没有

sentences.en: any friends because all I did was work and all I did was sit at home and that was my locked in crisis and then I kind of forced my way out I kind of like violently crossed that
sentences.zh: 任何朋友，因为我所有的生活就是工作，所有的生活就是坐在家里，那就是我的“被锁在内”危机，然后我有点强迫自己走出来，我有点像

sentences.en: threshold by just seriously having a pep talk with myself and being like hey you don't want this get out of here and what followed was this waiting room period where I felt good
